t5_blind_action.detail: THE TRAP, measured: UIA published the tab at physical (588,358); the DPI-unaware executor was handed exactly that, its own GetCursorPos then REPORTED (588,358) — the virtualization lies to the process about its own miss — while the real cursor sat at (735,448) (=x1.25). Tab stayed [selected=False]: MISS. Calibration probe: ask (320,320), land (400,400) -> scale 1.25 measured (not assumed). Corrected hand-off (470.4,286.4) logical -> landed (588,358) physical exactly -> tab flipped [selected=True]: HIT, verified in-channel before any screenshot.

measurements.notes: Closes DEEPENING-PLAN P1-Windows: the trap is now DEMONSTRATED, not just encoded. Three lessons with numbers: (1) the naive miss is invisible from inside the unaware process (own GetCursorPos echoes the asked coords; LOGPIXELSX reads 96 under 120) — only an independent aware reader sees (735,448); (2) the calibration is one move-and-measure round-trip (~150 ms) and yields the exact scale, mirroring the sandbox click-dpr.html finding: MEASURE the box->input scale, never hardcode /DPR; (3) the safety precondition (predicted-landing-inside-harmless-zone) aborted the first attempt against Calculator — mis-scaled clicks land 25% down-right of target, far enough to leave the window entirely; routers must bound the blast radius before any uncalibrated click. Scaling restored in a finally block: 96 DPI re-verified. Windows-vs-macOS symmetry now complete: same trap class, opposite direction (macOS CDP: device-px boxes fed to CSS-px input, divide; Windows: physical-px boxes fed to a virtualized executor, divide) — one self-calibration probe covers both.

runtime_verification.method: in-channel selected-state before/after each click + independent aware-process GetCursorPos as ground truth for where clicks actually landed
runtime_verification.agreement: naive: channel and cursor agree it missed; calibrated: landed exactly on target, state flipped
